subject: ventures/backyard-egg-profit-calculator
professional: a poultry extension specialist / small-flock farm business adviser who helps backyard sellers price eggs; first checks: is feed about 0.25 lb a hen a day and charged for every bird on the feed bill (not only the layers), does feed per dozen land near the 4 to 5 lb small flocks run, is the lay rate a flock-average hen-day figure with the seasonal and age decline, are replacement pullets costed with rearing feed and mortality, and are egg-sale rules (state egg laws, cartons, labels, refrigeration) framed as 'check your state' rather than implied safe at small scale

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the defaults and four scenarios by hand in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/53ffa676-4533-50af-a1cf-f7db84c8cb92/scratchpad/egg/re.mjs (no engine import): 20 x 0.70 x 365 = 5,110 eggs; 425.83 doz x 0.92 = 391.77 sold; feed 20 x 0.25 lb (the extension quarter pound a hen a day, e.g. University of Minnesota and Penn State small-flock guides) x 365 x $0.45 = $821.25; other $360; replacement 20 x $8 / 2 = $80; cartons $137.12; cash cost $1,398.37, $3.57/doz, 0.53 h/doz, margin $560.46, $2.69/h, wage price (1,398.37 + 3,120) / 391.77 = $11.53. Feed x2: $13.63 and -$1.25/h; lay 35%: $6.79 and $22.72; dark winter ($4, $0.60, 45%, 15%): $6.95 and -$3,805.69; $10 price: $12.11/h. All match the engine, the page (Playwright) and the guide. Feed conversion cross-check: 1,825 lb / 425.8 doz laid = 4.29 lb feed per dozen, inside the 4-5 lb small-flock range. The wrong number is the one the tool's own guidance produces: the 'Hens in lay' note (engine.mjs:18) tells the user to count only laying birds ('a flock of 20 on the fence is often 14 in the nest boxes'), but feed and replacement are charged only on that count (engine.mjs:63,65). Same 3,577 eggs either way: 14 in lay at 70% gives $3.96/doz and $1.37/h; 20 birds fed at 49% flock lay gives $4.95/doz and $0.07/h, so following the note understates cash cost per dozen by 20% and overstates profit per hour 20-fold. Reading the code alone would cap this at 2; it was run.
evidence.completeness: Walked every claimed feature in Chromium at 375 px (Playwright over python3 -m http.server, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/53ffa676-4533-50af-a1cf-f7db84c8cb92/scratchpad/egg/pw.cjs): Calculate gives the summary and 15 totals rows ($1,398.37, 392 dozen, $3.57, 0.53 h, $2.69/h, -$2,559.54, $3.57 breakeven, $11.53 wage price); price, feed and lay scenario tables render (lay 35/52.5/70/80.5%); dark-winter button gives $6.95/doz and a loss of $3,805.69; blank hens, 120% lay and 0 hours show named errors; usage counter {calculate_run:2, example_loaded:1}; opt-out removes the counters and sets the flag; no horizontal scroll (scrollWidth 375); guide page loads; no console errors. Copy summary not exercised (clipboard). No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/backyard-egg-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 14 tests, 14 pass, 61 ms. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (replacement without /layYears, cartons on eggs laid, loss guard >= -> >), 3 survived: summarize() verdict keyed on cash margin instead of after-wage (the default summary would then call a $2,559.54 loss 'a margin of'), the top lay-scenario factor 1.15 -> 1.5, and costPerEgg without the sold share (it is computed but never read). The page tests check that the guide's numbers match the engine, which keeps docs honest, but nothing tests the summary sentence on the default case or the input-note guidance that drives the feed count.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (118 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, both test files. Pure functions, one engine shared by page and guide tests, named-input errors instead of silent defaults (blank fields throw), escaped HTML, guarded localStorage, DNT/GPC honoured. Defects: costPerEgg is dead (engine.mjs:85); on an input error render() returns without hiding the previous result card, so stale results sit under an error (index.html:160-163); the section is headed 'What's recognised' (a template leftover for an input guide); fractional hens (20.5) accepted; with every cost zero the summary says 'feed is the largest cash line at 0.0%'.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-warranty, not-advice and non-affiliation footers on both pages (page.test.mjs); 'nothing is uploaded' (no fetch/XHR/beacon, asserted); local-only events named accurately; every worked number in the guide and index FAQ matches the engine (page.test.mjs and my hand build); README formulas match engine.mjs; served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin in llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals (the github.io links in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy, source-only). Not backed or unsafely framed: the 'dark winter' button and guide say a winter 'loses $3,805.69 a year', but that is a full year at 45% lay, not one winter; the guide says 'Check your state's rules on selling eggs, cartons and labelling before you scale up' (how-much-to-charge-for-a-dozen-eggs.html:63), which implies small sales need no check, while many state egg laws require registration, new or relabelled cartons and refrigeration at any scale; the other-cost note lists 'a cottage-food ... licence', but shell eggs usually fall under state egg laws and are excluded from many cottage-food laws.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a seller with 20 birds deciding what to charge. The cash and hours build-up, wage price and sensitivity tables give a usable first price, and the page is clear on a phone. But a real backyard flock always carries non-layers (pullets, moulting and older hens) and the tool tells the user to leave them out, which flatters the result most in exactly the winter case it advertises; there is no seasonal mix (summer and winter rates in one year), no mortality or rearing feed in replacements, so a professional would re-key the flock before quoting a price.
evidence.domain: Compared with extension small-flock guidance (about 0.25 lb layer feed a hen a day; 4-5 lb feed per dozen for small flocks; production breeds near 80-90% hen-day at peak, falling roughly 10-20% each later year and sharply in short days and moult; pullet cost = chick + about 20 weeks of rearing feed). Sound: feed rate, feed held constant when lay falls (hens eat anyway), loss share charged to sold dozens, cartons per dozen sold, own labour priced separately from cash margin. Departures: feed and replacement charged only on birds in lay while the note says to exclude non-layers; single annual lay rate, with the 'dark winter' scenario applied to all 365 days; replacement ignores mortality and spent-hen value (disclosed in README); $8 default pullet is low against chick plus rearing feed (defaults are labelled invented); egg-sale rules mentioned only as 'check your state', with cottage-food framing that usually does not apply to shell eggs.

defects.what: The 'Hens in lay' guidance tells the user to count only laying birds ('a flock of 20 on the fence is often 14 in the nest boxes'), but feed and replacement are charged only on that count, so the feed of pullets, moulting and broody hens disappears. Same 3,577 eggs: 14 in lay gives $3.96/doz and $1.37/h; 20 birds fed at 49% flock lay gives $4.95/doz and $0.07/h (cost per dozen 20% low, profit per hour 20x high). Worst in the winter case the tool advertises.

The 'dark winter' button and guide say a winter 'loses $3,805.69 a year', but the engine applies 45% lay and 60-cent feed to all 365 days; a reader takes it as the cost of one winter. No seasonal mix of summer and winter lay rates.

Three of six seeded mutants survive: the summary's profit/loss verdict can key on cash margin (the default would call a $2,559.54 loss 'a margin of') with every test green; the top lay-scenario factor and costPerEgg are unchecked.

Legal framing: 'Check your state's rules on selling eggs, cartons and labelling before you scale up' implies small sales need no check; many state egg laws require registration, clean or relabelled cartons and refrigeration at any scale. The other-cost note lists 'a cottage-food ... licence', though shell eggs usually sit under state egg laws and are excluded from many cottage-food laws.
On an input error render() returns without hiding the previous result card, so stale results stay on screen beneath the error.

Replacement cost ignores mortality, pullet rearing feed and spent-hen value; the $8 default pullet is below chick plus about 20 weeks of rearing feed (mortality is disclosed in the README; defaults are labelled invented).
costPerEgg is computed and never read; the input guide section is headed 'What's recognised' (template leftover); fractional hens accepted.

verdict: A small, clean and honest egg-pricing calculator whose arithmetic is right: the defaults ($1,398.37 cash a year, $3.57 and 0.53 hours a dozen, $2.69 an hour, $11.53 for a $15 wage) and every scenario the pages quote match a hand build-up from the extension quarter-pound feed rate, feed per dozen lands at a plausible 4.29 lb, and the page works on a phone with the disclaimer and local-only counting it describes. It does not meet the bar. Its own input guidance tells sellers to count only birds in lay, so the feed of non-layers vanishes and cost per dozen comes out about 20% low in exactly the winter case it advertises; the 'dark winter' loss is a full year at winter rates presented as a winter; the legal note says to check state rules 'before you scale up'; and half the seeded mutants survive, including the summary's profit-or-loss verdict. Rewording the hens note to 'every bird you feed' with a flock-average lay rate, reframing the winter scenario, and testing the summary verdict would lift correctness, claims and verification to 3.
